text:
Noah Rivera: FYI — noticed p99 on the account-summary dashboard spiked at 14:22 but the endpoint breakdown p99 stays steady. Timeline alignment looks identical. Anyone have quick theories?

Tess Huang: Quick suspects: (1) rollup method (merged tdigest) vs per-backend raw samples, (2) retries included in one view but filtered in the other, (3) routing fallback kicked in and moved a few percent to a slower pool.

Amir Desai: Also check smoothing/windowing. The small sparkline uses a 30s smoothing window; the percentile panel shows 10s buckets. That can make spikes appear shifted and not line up.

Noah Rivera: Good call. I pulled the raw query: 
```
/metrics?p=service:account-summary&agg=percentile(p99)&window=5m&bucket=10s
```
Endpoint pane uses `?source=backend_raw&retry_filter=exclude`.

Tess Huang: Oof. That retry_filter is probably the difference. If 1.5% of traffic retries and retries land on a slow replica, merged rollup that includes them will show tail blowups.

Amir Desai: UX idea: show an "origin transparency" micro-badge next to each percentile metric that displays three small flags: retries? ingress/backend? fallback%. Hover expands to a flyout with sample counts and a short explanation. Something like: 
- origins: ingress(120k) backend(119k) fallback(2.1k)
- retries_included: yes
- merge_method: tdigest(k=100)

Noah Rivera: Love that. Also add a quick action in the flyout: "Compare raw vs merged" which runs a canned internal query and shows both p99 numbers side-by-side with cost estimate.

Tess Huang: From infra: merged tdigest can mask small slow shards unless we weight by shard sample count. Two engineering mitigations: (A) conditional increase of sketch resolution when total sample_count < threshold, (B) origin-aware correction factor where we compute per-shard p99 and take a weighted max. Both increase CPU/cost.

Amir Desai: Proposal for rollout: feature-flag the badge + flyout and the "compare" action behind internal-only ff. Add a telemetry job that injects 2% slow fanout daily and records merged_vs_raw p99 delta. If delta > 15% for 3 runs, promote a ticket.

Noah Rivera: Can we also auto-annotate timeseries when routing weight or quota fallback events occur? Annotation payload: event_type, affected_pct, policy_id, trace_link. That would make the "why did p99 change" flow much faster.

Sam Ops: deploy-bot: canary deploy started "console/origin-badge-v1" at 1818888990 :rocket:

Tess Huang: API suggestion: add GET /internal/telemetry/origin_metadata?svc=...&start=... which returns light provenance per-bucket: ["bucket_ts","ingress_count","backend_count","fallback_count","retries_included"] — string values only for now. Gate to internal console.

Amir Desai: I'll sketch the telemetry job and a cheap unit test that simulates retry-heavy traffic and verifies the compare action surfaces the delta. Also adding a weekly alert if merged_sketch_p99 - raw_p99 > 12% for 7d.

Noah Rivera: Great. Tess, Amir, can you PR the ff + flyout copy? I'll prep a short runbook snippet for oncall: "If p99 mismatch, open flyout -> run compare -> check routing/quotas -> link to traces." Keep the runbook ~5 bullets.

deploy-bot: canary deployed "console/origin-badge-v1" at 1818889022 :white_check_mark:

Tess Huang: I'll post mockups in #design after lunch and tag @Noah for copy review.

Noah Rivera: Thanks all. If the canary looks clean we can flip ff to internal-only tomorrow and schedule telemetry checks. This should cut a bunch of noisy p99 pages. :thumbsup:
